newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Merrill says ex-banker case costs not significant.
newsitem.headline: Merrill says ex-banker case costs not significant.

text.p: U.S. securities house Merrill Lynch said it did not expect to incur significant costs arising from the case of an ex-employee under investigation for alleged fraud.
A company spokesman in Hong Kong told Reuters by telephone that "any of the costs incurred in this matter will not be significant to Merrill Lynch's business or financial position".

The U.S. securities house has said the former employee, private client financial consultant Kevin Wallace, had "engaged in unauthorised trading, misrepresenting or falsifying private clients' statements and forging client signatures".
It also has said it started civil proceedings in Singapore and Hong Kong against Wallace, and filed a criminal complaint in Singapore.
A lawsuit filed in the Singapore High Court by Merrill against Wallace has been sealed to protect confidential customer accounts.

Merrill has not commented on the amount in question in the case but industry sources and media reports have estimated some US$30 million could be involved. Merrill made US$1.6 billion in profits last year.
Singapore's Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) said on Thursday it was continuing its probe of the case.
"We can confirm that we have received the reports and that we're looking into the matter," a spokeswoman had said earlier.
The CAD, Singapore's white collar crime unit, is expected to examine the details of the case to decide if there was evidence of criminal activity, a legal source said.
Wallace was dismissed by the company on May 15, and last reported in Hong Kong. Efforts to reach him there and in Singapore have been unsuccessful.
